candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 16:1-35. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. Jude 11.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On the swallowing of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram by the earth (Num 16:32), Ephrem reads the judgment-against-priestly-rebellion as the canonical anchor of the gravity-of-priesthood: those who usurp the priestly office without divine appointment fall through the very earth that should bear them. Korah's rebellion is doubled in Jude 11 ('perished in the gainsaying of Core') and read as type of every later schismatic seizure of office. Tewahedo canon-law cites Num 16:32 + Jude 11 as the canonical doubled-warrant for the gravity of unauthorised priesthood; only the lawfully-ordained may approach the tabot.
